[Back to the lesson](embedding-space.qmd) · [Learning path plan](review-path.qmd#representations)

## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- For a vocabulary of size V and embedding dimension d, the embedding matrix has shape V × d. ID i selects row i.
- The ID is a row index. The d learned numbers stored in the row are the embedding coordinates.
- With fixed parameters, two occurrences of the same ID share the lookup vector. States produced later can differ with position and context.

## Predict before checking {#revision-check}

Consider the toy ID sequence $[17,42,8,17]$, with zero-based sequence positions. Which rows does the table read, and in what order? Which vector must repeat if the table stays fixed?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

The rows read are $E_{17,:}$, $E_{42,:}$, $E_{8,:}$, and $E_{17,:}$, in that order. Both occurrences of ID 17 retrieve the same initial vector. In the [first-block-input exercise](exercises/text-data.qmd#ex-token-to-block-input), that vector is fixed at $(2,-1)$; the other values are not needed to establish the order.

If the IDs are replaced by a permutation and the corresponding table rows are moved in the same way, lookup returns the same vectors. Renumbering IDs without permuting the table instead changes the rows that are read. This lookup-level invariance does not by itself preserve a complete model: the other vocabulary-indexed parameters must also be permuted consistently.

IDs 41 and 42 do not necessarily have nearby vectors: proximity between vocabulary indices places no constraint on the geometry of the learned rows.

</details>

[Work through the lookup exercise](exercises/text-data.qmd#ex-text-to-embedding-lookup) to check the row order, then predict what happens when IDs are renumbered with or without the corresponding table-row permutation.
